title: Introduce RAG step replayer authoring sandbox with streamed probes and telemetry harness
author: Maya Thompson
release_notes: Adds a lightweight RAG authoring sandbox that replays stepwise sessions, captures streamed telemetry probes, and includes a devcontainer for local onboarding. Recommended for teams building iterated retrieval/agent workflows.
description:
Motivation: Authoring RAG workflows interactively is hard to debug when steps are non-deterministic or tools return partial/streamed outputs. This quickstart provides a small, local-first sandbox that can record and replay stepwise RAG sessions, attach streamed probes (telemetry events, intermediate embeddings, tool call traces), and surface them in a compact trace viewer. The goal is to help prompt/contract authors iterate on step boundaries, tool contracts, and retrieval strategies without running full end-to-end infra.

What this PR does (single-string description): Adds a new quickstart under quickstarts/step-replayer that contains: a README with step-by-step authoring guidance, a devcontainer for one-click onboarding, a minimal local replayer binary (node script) that can ingest recorded sessions and replay them with configurable time dilation, a probes YAML schema plus sample probes emitter, a small set of example prompt/step fixtures, and an instrumentation shim that emits compact telemetry to stdout or to an optional local HTTP sink. Also updates docs/quickstarts/index.yml to surface the new quickstart in the docs site navigation.

Why now: Several internal experiments (ENG-4832) surfaced the need for deterministic replay when evaluating prompt variants across retrieval configurations. This quickstart encapsulates those patterns and makes it easier to add step-level assertions for regressions.

Checklist (author):
- [x] Quickstart scaffolding and README with walkthrough and expected outcomes
- [x] Devcontainer and small Dockerfile for reproducible local runs
- [x] Telemetry probes schema and emitter examples
- [x] Step replayer script and replay fixtures
- [x] Docs index entry and short landing copy
- [x] Basic smoke tests in CI (local run path)

Usage notes: The replayer supports two modes: record (wraps a live session and emits a compact JSONL trace) and replay (replays a trace and optionally emits the same stream of probes to a test harness). The README documents how to wire the emitter to a local HTTP probe-sink and how to assert on intermediate embeddings or tool-call payloads. There is also a sample 'contract-checks.json' that demonstrates how to fail a replay run if certain tool call outputs deviate.

Security/Privacy: The quickstart defaults to local-only storage and provides guidance in README for sanitizing PII before recording. There are no remote telemetry endpoints enabled by default.

Backward compatibility: The replayer uses a compact trace schema with an explicit version key (trace_schema_v: "1.0"). Future schema changes will be opt-in.

Related work: Builds on patterns from recent authoring labs and tool-contract proposals. References: ENG-4832, PM-221.

CI/Testing instructions: CI includes a lightweight smoke job that spins up the devcontainer, runs the replayer against a recorded fixture in replay mode and verifies a set of assertion hooks. E2E is intentionally excluded from main CI to keep runtime small.

Merge notes: Squash-merged after approvals and a successful CI run.

testing_instructions: 1) Open repo in the provided devcontainer. 2) Run npm ci in quickstarts/step-replayer. 3) Start sample emitter: node probes/sample-emitter.js --sink stdout. 4) Run replayer in replay mode: node replayer/index.js --replay fixtures/sample-trace.jsonl --assert contract-checks.json --stub-network. 5) Observe probes printed to stdout or forwarded to local HTTP sink. 6) See README for advanced assertions and CI integration.
